'''Elsa Reichmanis''' (born 9 December 1953 in Melbourne, Australia)<ref name="OH">{{cite web|author=Center for Oral History| title= Elsa Reichmanis |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/oral-histories/reichmanis-elsa|website= [[Science History Institute]] }}</ref><ref name="transcript">{{cite book|first=David C. |last=Brock|title=Elsa Reichmanis, Transcript of an Interview Conducted by David C. Brock at Murray Hill, New Jersey on 1 August 2001 |date=1 August 2001 |url=https://oh.sciencehistory.org/sites/default/files/reichmanis_e_0222_suppl.pdf|place=Philadelphia, PA|publisher=[[Science History Institute|Chemical Heritage Foundation]] }}</ref> is an American chemist, who was the 2003 president of the [[American Chemical Society]]. She was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]] in 1995 for the discovery, development, and engineering leadership of new families of lithographic materials and processes that enable VLSI manufacturing. She was also inducted into the [[National Academy of Inventors]] in 2020. She is currently the Anderson Endowed Chair in Chemical and Biomolecular Engineering at [[Lehigh University]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Groundbreaking Scholar Elsa Reichmanis to Join Faculty at Lehigh|url=https://www2.lehigh.edu/news/groundbreaking-scholar-elsa-reichmanis-to-join-faculty-at-lehigh|date=2019-11-07|website=Lehigh University|language=en|access-date=2020-05-30}}</ref> She previously served on the faculty at The [[Georgia Tech|Georgia Institute of Technology]]. Reichmanis is noted for her research into [[microlithography]], and is credited for contributing to the "development of a fundamental molecular level understanding of how chemical structure affects materials function leading to new families of lithographic materials and processes that may enable advanced [[VLSI]] manufacturing".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://reichmanis.chbe.gatech.edu/reichmanis.html|title=Elsa Reichmanis|publisher=Elsa Reichmanis Research group|access-date=10 September 2015|archive-date=25 December 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225084626/http://reichmanis.chbe.gatech.edu/reichmanis.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==Education==
Reichmanis completed her bachelor's degree in chemistry in 1972 and her [[Doctor of Philosophy|PhD]] in [[organic chemistry]] in 1975, both at [[Syracuse University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://lemelson.mit.edu/resources/elsa-reichmanis|title=Elsa Reichmanis - Chemically Amplified Resists|publisher=Lemelson MIT|access-date=2020-02-29}}</ref>

== Awards and honors ==
Reichmanis' awards and honors include:

*1992: R&D 100 Award from Research and Development Magazine<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.rdworldonline.com/rd-100-archive/1992/|title=R&D 100 Archive of Winners - 1992|access-date=2020-02-29}}</ref>
*1993: Achievement Award from the [[Society of Women Engineers]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://oldswesite.swe.org/news-archive/154-awards/657-past-award-recipients-achievement|title=Achievement Award Recipients|access-date=2020-02-29}}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref>
*1995: Elected a Member of the [[National Academy of Engineering]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Dr. Elsa Reichmanis | publisher=National Academy of Engineering|url=https://www.nae.edu/MembersSection/MemberDirectory/30003.aspx|access-date=11 July 2022}}</ref>
*1997: Elected [[Fellow of the American Association for the Advancement of Science]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/fellows/listing|title=AAAS - Elected Fellows|access-date=2020-02-29}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.aaas.org/membership/member-spotlight/elsa-reichmanis-forges-powerful-bonds-collaboration|title=Elsa Reichmanis Forges Powerful Bonds of Collaboration|access-date=2020-02-29}}</ref>
*2001: [[Perkin Medal]]<ref>{{cite journal|title=Elsa Reichmanis Wins Perkin Medal|journal=Chemistry International |date=1 July 2001|volume=23|issue=4|doi=10.1515/ci.2001.23.4.117a|doi-access=free}}</ref>
*2018: Elected a Fellow of the [[Materials Research Society]]<ref>{{cite web|title=List of MRS Fellows|url=https://www.mrs.org/mrs-fellows-list|publisher=Materials Research Society|access-date=6 March 2019|archive-date=10 February 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200210191938/http://mrs.org/mrs-fellows-list|url-status=dead}}</ref>
*2018: [[American Chemical Society|ACS]] Award in the Chemistry of Materials<ref>{{cite web|url=https://pmsedivision.org/acs-tcom/|title=ACS Award in the Chemistry of Materials|publisher=American Chemical Society - Division of Polymeric Materials: Science and Engineering|access-date=2020-02-29}}</ref>
*2020: Elected a Fellow of the [[National Academy of Inventors]]<ref>{{cite web|title=Elsa Reichmanis elected Fellow of the National Academy of Inventors|url=https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2020-12/lu-ere120820.php|publisher=EurekAlert!, [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]]|date=2020-12-08|access-date=2020-12-11}}</ref>
